summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old male with a history of end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, coronary artery disease, diabetes, and peripheral vascular disease was admitted for evaluation of melena present for four days, associated with occasional lightheadedness and right upper quadrant abdominal pain radiating to the back. Initial workup revealed guaiac-positive stools but a negative nasogastric lavage. An ultrasound showed cholelithiasis without cholecystitis. During the emergency department stay, he developed transient substernal chest pain typical of angina, which resolved with sublingual nitroglycerin and morphine; cardiac enzymes were negative. He underwent an upper endoscopy that revealed erosive gastritis without active bleeding. He was started on intravenous pantoprazole and discharged on oral esomeprazole 40 mg twice daily. An H. pylori antibody test was negative. A capsule endoscopy was scheduled for outpatient follow-up. His cardiac and renal medications were continued without change, and he was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to return for any recurrent bleeding, chest pain, or other concerning symptoms.
problems: Unspecified gastritis and gastroduodenitis, without mention of hemorrhage
Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
